name: Domaine de la Mordorée Lirac Cuvée de la Reine des Bois 2019
text:
## Domaine de la Mordorée Lirac Cuvée de la Reine des Bois 2019

**The story.** Domaine de la Mordorée is young by Châteauneuf standards. It was founded in 1986 by two brothers, Christophe and Fabrice Delorme, with just 5 hectares of vines, and they grew it quickly into one of the leading estates of the southern Rhône, with vineyards in [Châteauneuf-du-Pape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC), [Lirac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lirac_AOC), [Tavel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tavel_AOC) and the [Côtes du Rhône](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B4tes_du_Rh%C3%B4ne_AOC). Christophe died far too young, on 10 June 2015, and in September 2017 Fabrice stepped back from running the domaine, though he remained a shareholder ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/mordoree-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).

The name comes from the [woodcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurasian_woodcock), a wild game bird of the forests, which is why a woodcock appears on the label. In the same spirit, the estate's top Châteauneuf, first made in 1996, is called La Reine des Bois: "the Queen of the Woods". The vineyards have been farmed [organically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_farming) for years and were certified 100% organic in 2013 ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/mordoree-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).

**The vineyards.** In Châteauneuf the estate owns 12.7 hectares in some of the best sites: [La Crau](https://www.google.com/maps?q=La+Crau,+Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape,+France&t=k), Bois la Ville and Cabrières. La Crau is the famous plateau of big rounded stones, the [galets roulés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galets_roul%C3%A9s), and Mordorée has vines there over 100 years old ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/mordoree-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)). The stones soak up the sun by day and give the heat back to the vines at night ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).

**The wine: La Reine des Bois.** This is the estate's flagship, from La Crau vines averaging about 60 years old, on pure stony soil. It is mostly [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache) (70 to 80%), with [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre), [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), [Cinsault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinsaut) and [Vaccarèse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brun_Argent%C3%A9). The grapes are fully destemmed, and the wine is aged partly in tanks and partly in French oak barrels; the share of new oak has fallen over the years, and for the 2018 Jeb Dunnuck reports only older barrels were used. About 1,500 cases are made ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/mordoree-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/); Jeb Dunnuck via [Kysela](https://kysela.com/press/wine-reviews-news/372-mordoree-chateauneuf-du-pape-rouge-reine-bois/5868-2018-domaine-de-la-mordoree-chateauneuf-du-pape-cuvee-de-la-reine-des-bois-95-pts-jd.html)).

**The wine: Lirac La Reine des Bois.** Across the [Rhône](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rh%C3%B4ne) from Châteauneuf, in [Lirac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lirac_AOC), Mordorée makes a red "Queen of the Woods" that critics regularly rank among the best wines of the appellation. Unusually, it is roughly equal parts [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache), [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah) and [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre), from vines around 40 years old on [galets roulés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galets_roul%C3%A9s) over sand and red clay, farmed organically and now certified [biodynamic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodynamic_agriculture) by [Demeter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demeter_International). It macerates for 30 days, about 10% ferments in used casks and the rest in steel, and around 15% ages a year in oak; production is about 2,400 cases (only 1,800 in 2020 and 2,000 in 2019). The importer suggests grilled meats, meats in sauce, game birds, rabbit and semi-mature cheeses ([Kysela](https://kysela.com/mordoree-lirac-rouge-la-reine-des-bois.html)).

**The vintage.** 2019 was a scorching, drought year across the southern Rhône ([2019 European heatwaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_European_heatwaves)). [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/southern-rhone) says the reds are powerful, with more tannin than usual, surprisingly fresh acidity and warming alcohol, and that most will improve with age.

**What the critics say for 2019.** Via the US importer, [Kysela](https://kysela.com/mordoree-lirac-rouge-la-reine-des-bois.html):
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck): 92 to 94** (October 2020, [review](https://kysela.com/press/wine-reviews-news/379-mordoree-lirac-rouge-reine-des-bois/5866-2019-domaine-de-la-mordoree-lirac-rouge-la-reine-des-bois-92-94-pts-jd.html)). 40% Syrah and 30% each Mourvèdre and Grenache: cassis, framboise, pepper, graphite and smoked meat; full-bodied and seamless with great tannins. "Always in the running for the Lirac of the vintage, and bests many a top Châteauneuf du Pape." Needs 2 to 3 years; a 10 to 15-year wine.
- **[James Suckling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Suckling): 94** (February 2022, [review](https://kysela.com/press/wine-reviews-news/379-mordoree-lirac-rouge-reine-des-bois/6858-2019-domaine-de-la-mordoree-lirac-rouge-la-reine-des-bois-94-pts-js.html)). "Stunningly fresh and pure forest-berry and herb aromas"; rich yet beautifully proportioned, silky and long.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 89.4** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is seven years old. Dunnuck gave it 10 to 15 years, so it is in its drinking window with plenty of time. Decant an hour ahead.

**Serving.** The Wine Cellar Insider suggests about 15.5°C, almost cellar temperature, for freshness and lift, and 1 to 2 hours in a [decanter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decantation) for younger bottles; older ones need only enough to leave the sediment behind. It says Mordorée is usually best with 4 to 7 years in bottle, and the best vintages drink well for up to 25 years ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/mordoree-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).

**Food.** The Wine Cellar Insider suggests classic meat dishes (veal, pork, beef, lamb, duck, game, roast chicken, braises, sausages, grilled meats, barbecue and [cassoulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassoulet)), plus mushrooms, cheese, eggplant and tomatoes. Given the woodcock on the label, game is the natural choice: roast pheasant or [venison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venison), [wild boar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_boar) stew, or a [rack of lamb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rack_of_lamb) with garlic and thyme. I'd avoid delicate fish and very spicy food.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the three stores on this site lists La Reine des Bois at the moment. It turns up with merchants such as [JJ Buckley](https://www.jjbuckley.com/) and [Fine+Rare](https://www.frw.co.uk/), and at auction. Mordorée's other wines are easier to find: BC Liquor carries another of the estate's Châteauneufs at $105.99, and BSW Liquor and ZYN carry its [Tavel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tavel_AOC) rosé and [Lirac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lirac_AOC) wines from about $44 to $64. For a wine regularly scored in the mid to high 90s, it is fairly priced among top Châteauneufs.

**From the history books**
- **The popes and their castle.** In 1309 [Pope Clement V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Clement_V) moved the papacy to [Avignon](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Palais+des+Papes,+Avignon,+France&t=k), beginning the [Avignon Papacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon_Papacy). His successor [John XXII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_XXII) improved the vineyards to the north and built the summer [castle](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Ch%C3%A2teau+des+Papes,+Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape,+France&t=k) that gave the village its name, "the Pope's new castle" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **France's first appellation.** Fraud was so common in the early 20th century that local growers, led by Baron [Pierre Le Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Le_Roy_de_Boiseaumari%C3%A9) of [Château Fortia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_Fortia), drew up France's first [appellation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellation_d'origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e) rules in 1923, made law in 1936 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **Tavel, the rosé village.** Jeff Leve calls Mordorée's [Tavel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tavel_AOC) rosé "sublime" ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/mordoree-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)). Tavel, across the [Rhône](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rh%C3%B4ne) from Châteauneuf, is an appellation for rosé only ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lirac_AOC)).
- **Lirac, the right bank.** Much of the rest of the estate lies across the river in [Lirac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lirac_AOC) ([see it from above](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Lirac,+Gard,+France&t=k)), one of the 13 crus of the Rhône Valley, on low hills along the right bank ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lirac_AOC)).

**Curious details**
- **The painter's feather returns.** La Plume du Peintre ("the painter's feather") is the estate's rarest cuvée, made only in exceptional years. Jeff Leve reported that after Christophe Delorme's death the family said it would not be made again ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/mordoree-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)), but it has since returned: Jeb Dunnuck gave the 2019 Châteauneuf Plume du Peintre 98+ ([Kysela](https://kysela.com/mordoree-chateauneuf-du-pape-rouge-la-plume-du-peintre.html)).
- **Skipping great years.** The estate chose not to make La Plume du Peintre in the great 2007, 2009 or 2010 vintages, so as not to take the best grapes away from La Reine des Bois.
- **A second wine since 2014.** La Belle Voyageuse ("the beautiful traveller"), launched in 2014, works as the second wine of La Reine des Bois, which Jeff Leve says should lift the quality of the flagship.
- **The flying-cigar law.** In 1954, after local reports of [UFOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_saucer), the Châteauneuf council banned "flying cigars" from flying over or landing in the commune. The decree is still in force ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **Why the blend matters.** In Châteauneuf, [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache) gives sweet, ripe, almost jam-like juice when very ripe; [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah) adds colour and spice; and [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre) brings elegance and structure. Grenache covered about 72% of the appellation's vineyards in 2004, Syrah about 10.5% and Mourvèdre only about 7% ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **Strong by law.** Châteauneuf must reach at least 12.5% alcohol with no added sugar, and most wines come in at 14 to 15.5%. Yields are limited to 35 hectolitres per hectare, nearly half what Bordeaux allows ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC); [Bordeaux wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux_wine)).
